irregularities.statement: Two documents in this repository state DIFFERENT marginal bars for the same metric. src/gems32/metric.py and the passing test tests/test_metric.py::test_marginal_emission_rule_exact_single_truth_pixel say k > alpha*s = 0.0520 at s = 0.26. docs/research/score-ceiling-analysis.md section 1 states k > alpha*s/(1 - alpha*s) = 0.0549. The latter form does not follow from the metric: adding one unit of mass raises the denominator by EXACTLY alpha regardless of where it lands, giving k > alpha*s. A brute-force sweep over 300 random configurations agrees with the alpha*s form 300/300.
irregularities.mitigation: The exact theorem is stated, machine-verified in scripts/verify_theorems.py block (B), and used by src/gems32/emitter.py. NOTE the propagated consequence: the successor repository GEMSDOE28 uses tau_live = 0.05485 as its live break-even efficiency, which is 5.5% too high, biasing its pruning rule toward deleting dots that were still profitable.

irregularities.statement: The 'adaptive credit bar' that this project has repeatedly cited as its stopping rule CANNOT BIND on an emission confined to its own belief support. For a support pixel of a binary field, kbar(x) = sum_delta field(x+delta)k(delta) >= field(x)k(0) = 1, so the added false-positive mass 1 - kbar <= 0 and the acceptance inequality holds unconditionally for any s < 1/alpha = 5. Measured: emitter.emit(field, budget=None, prior_dti=0.26) consumes the ENTIRE 121,131-px H19-5 support and terminates with stopped_by='exhausted_support'.
irregularities.mitigation: Stated openly in knowledge/02 section 4b. The bar is still the correct rule for deciding whether a dot PAYS; it is simply not a constraint on an emission that never leaves its own support. Budget must therefore come from somewhere else -- which is exactly why the three-slot identification experiment that measures the hidden-set quantities is the next action rather than another budget sweep.

irregularities.statement: Several live README/site passages and docs/research/score-ceiling-analysis.md used an incorrect DTI denominator simplification (0.8*T + 0.2*|P| + 0.8*|G|) and treated alpha*s/(1-alpha*s) as the universal marginal inclusion threshold. The exact metric is T/(T + alpha*FP + beta*FN) = T/(alpha*(T+S-M)+beta*|G|). For a single new pixel contributing its full kernel credit to previously uncovered truth, the idealized threshold is k>alpha*s; partially covered fields require the actual delta TP/FP/FN condition. Prior exact hidden TP/recall/score-ceiling claims derived from the bad identity are withdrawn.
